questions.q: What is the purpose of the features {} block inside provider "azurerm"?
options: It lists which Azure resource types the configuration is allowed to create
It is required by the azurerm provider, even empty, and configures provider-wide behaviors
It stores the service principal's secret
It enables preview features in the Azure Portal
questions.explain: The azurerm provider requires a features {} block even when empty; it's where provider-wide behaviors can be overridden.

questions.q: Which authentication method is most appropriate for a CI/CD pipeline with no human present to sign in?
options: Azure CLI with az login
A service principal (or OIDC workload identity) authenticated via environment variables
Typing a password into the terraform apply prompt
Authentication is not required for terraform apply
questions.explain: Service principals and OIDC workload identity federation are designed for non-interactive authentication, which is what a pipeline needs.

questions.q: What does the version = "~> 3.90" constraint on the azurerm provider do?
options: Forces Terraform to use exactly version 3.90.0 and nothing else
Pins the provider to the 3.90.x line, allowing patch updates but blocking a breaking major version
Sets the Azure API version used by all resources
Has no effect unless terraform init is run with a flag
questions.explain: The ~> pessimistic constraint operator allows patch-level updates within 3.90.x while blocking an upgrade to 4.x.

questions.q: What does subscription_id in the provider "azurerm" block actually determine?
options: Which identity Terraform authenticates as
Which Azure subscription resources are provisioned into
Which Terraform Cloud workspace is used
The region every resource defaults to
questions.explain: subscription_id targets a specific Azure subscription; it does not establish identity, which is handled separately by az login, a service principal, or OIDC.

questions.q: After running az login and az account set, what does terraform init do?
options: Creates all the resources defined in the configuration
Downloads and installs the azurerm provider plugin matching the version constraint
Deletes any existing Azure resources that aren't in the configuration
Logs the user out of the Azure CLI
questions.explain: terraform init downloads the provider plugins declared in required_providers; it does not create or destroy any Azure resources.
